unit.title: Health & weather
canDo: Describe the weather today and tomorrow
Say where it hurts and what you need
Tell someone not to do something with -지 마세요

lessons.title: Hot, cold, clear, cloudy
lessons.goal: Use rain, snow, wind and the four everyday weather adjectives

lessons.title: It hurts here
lessons.goal: Name body parts, say what hurts and say what you must do

lessons.title: At the pharmacy
lessons.goal: Understand symptoms and advice, and hear what not to do

lessons.title: Today's weather and your body
lessons.goal: Read a short forecast and match each day to the right advice

lessons.title: Weather, body, advice
lessons.goal: Describe weather, say what hurts, and give or refuse advice without hints

grammar.label: if / when (-면)
grammar.explanation: Attach -면 to a verb or adjective stem for 'if' or 'when': 비가 오면, 아프면. The second clause gives the result or the advice.

examples.en: If it rains, use an umbrella.
If you feel sick, go to the hospital.

grammar.label: will / probably (-겠-)
grammar.explanation: -겠- adds the speaker's intention or a careful guess. In weather talk it means 'it looks like it will…'; in 알겠어요 it means 'understood'.

grammar.label: must (-아/어야 해요)
grammar.explanation: Use -아/어야 해요 when something is necessary: 먹어야 해요, 가야 해요. 하다 verbs become 해야 해요.

examples.en: I have to go to bed early today.

grammar.label: don't (-지 마세요)
grammar.explanation: Attach -지 마세요 to a verb stem for a polite 'please don't': 가지 마세요, 걱정하지 마세요. It is the negative of -(으)세요.
grammar.mistake: 안 마시지 마세요 ✗ (double negative) → 마시지 마세요 ✓

sentences.english: The sky is clear today. I'm going to take photos.
sentences.literal: Today, the sky is clear. Photos take-will.
distractors: The sky is cloudy today. I'm going to take photos.
The sky is clear today. I'm not going to take photos.
The sky was clear yesterday. I took photos.
sentences.notes: The subject marker 이 follows 하늘 because it ends in a consonant.

sentences.english: If it rains, you have to buy an umbrella.
sentences.literal: If rain comes, an umbrella buy-must.
distractors: If it rains, you have to buy a mask.
If it snows, you have to buy an umbrella.
If it rains, you don't have to buy an umbrella.
sentences.notes: Korean says 'rain comes': 비가 와요, so the condition is 비가 오면.

sentences.korean: 여름에는 정말 더워요. 물을 많이 마셔야 해요.
sentences.romanization: yeoreumeneun jeongmal deowoyo. mureul mani masyeoya haeyo.
sentences.english: In summer it is really hot. You have to drink a lot of water.
sentences.literal: In summer, really it-is-hot. Water a lot drink-must.
distractors: In summer it is really cold. You have to drink a lot of water.
In summer it is really hot. You must not drink water.
In winter it is really hot. You have to drink a lot of water.
sentences.notes: 덥다 changes its ㅂ to 우: 덥 + 어요 = 더워요.

sentences.korean: 서울은 겨울에 아주 추워요. 따뜻하게 입어야 해요.
sentences.romanization: seoureun gyeoure aju chuwoyo. ttatteuthage ibeoya haeyo.
sentences.english: Seoul is very cold in winter. You have to dress warmly.
sentences.literal: As for Seoul, in winter very it-is-cold. Warmly dress-must.
distractors: Seoul is very cold in summer. You have to dress warmly.
Seoul is very cold in winter. You don't have to dress warmly.
Busan is very cold in winter. You have to dress warmly.
sentences.notes: 춥다 follows the same ㅂ rule: 춥 + 어요 = 추워요.

sentences.english: The wind is cool today. It would be nice to take a walk.
sentences.literal: Today, the wind is cool. Even walking would-be-good.
distractors: The wind is cold today. It would be nice to take a walk.
The wind is cool today. It would not be nice to take a walk.
The wind was cool yesterday. It was nice to take a walk.
sentences.notes: 시원해요 is the good kind of cool, like a breeze or a cold drink.

sentences.korean: 겨울에는 눈이 많이 와요. 운전하지 마세요.
sentences.romanization: gyeoureneun nuni mani wayo. unjeonhaji maseyo.
sentences.english: It snows a lot in winter. Don't drive.
sentences.literal: In winter, snow comes a lot. Do-not-drive.
distractors: It rains a lot in winter. Don't drive.
It snows a lot in summer. Don't drive.
It snows a lot in winter. Please drive carefully.
sentences.notes: 눈 is snow and also 'eye'. In weather sentences the subject marker makes it clear.

sentences.korean: 머리가 아파요. 이 약을 먹어야 해요.
sentences.romanization: meoriga apayo. i yageul meogeoya haeyo.
sentences.english: I have a headache. I have to take this medicine.
sentences.literal: The head hurts. This medicine eat-must.
distractors: I have a headache. I must not take this medicine.
My stomach hurts. I have to take this medicine.
I had a headache. I had to take this medicine.
sentences.notes: Korean says 'the head hurts', not 'I have a headache'. The body part is the subject.

sentences.korean: 목이 아프고 기침이 나서 집에서 쉬어야 해요.
sentences.romanization: moki apeugo gichimi naseo jibeseo swieoya haeyo.
sentences.english: My throat hurts and I have a cough, so I have to rest at home.
sentences.literal: Throat hurts-and, cough comes-because, at home rest-must.
distractors: My throat hurts and I have a cough, so I have to go to work.
My throat is fine and I have a cough, so I have to rest at home.
My head hurts and I have a cough, so I have to rest at home.
sentences.notes: 기침이 나다 is the fixed phrase for 'to cough'; the cough 'comes out'.

sentences.english: If you have a fever, you have to take medicine.
sentences.literal: If a fever exists, medicine eat-must.
distractors: If you have a fever, you must buy medicine.
If you have a cough, you must take medicine.
If you have a fever, you don't have to take medicine.
sentences.notes: Koreans 'eat' medicine: 약을 먹어요.

sentences.english: I have to buy medicine at the pharmacy.
sentences.literal: At the pharmacy, medicine buy-must.
distractors: I have to buy medicine at the hospital.
I bought medicine at the pharmacy.
I don't have to buy medicine.
sentences.notes: 사다 + -아야 해요 = 사야 해요. The ㄹ of the stem does not appear.

sentences.korean: 몸이 안 좋으면 따뜻한 물을 마셔야 해요.
sentences.romanization: momi an joeumyeon ttatteutan mureul masyeoya haeyo.
sentences.english: If you don't feel well, you have to drink warm water.
sentences.literal: If the body is not good, warm water drink-must.
distractors: If you don't feel well, you must drink cold water.
If you feel good, you have to drink warm water.
If you don't feel well, you must not drink water.
sentences.notes: Two endings stack here: 안 좋으면 sets the condition, 마셔야 해요 gives the duty.

sentences.english: For a cold, you have to wear a mask.
sentences.literal: For a cold, a mask wear-must.
distractors: For a cold, you don't have to wear a mask.
For a fever, you have to wear a mask.
For a cold, you have to take off your mask.
sentences.notes: 에는 here means 'for / in the case of', not a location.

sentences.korean: 오후에는 하늘이 흐려요. 우산을 준비해야 해요.
sentences.romanization: ohuneun haneuri heuryeoyo. usaneul junbihaeya haeyo.
sentences.english: In the afternoon the sky is cloudy. You have to get an umbrella ready.
sentences.literal: In the afternoon, the sky is cloudy. An umbrella prepare-must.
distractors: In the morning the sky is cloudy. You have to get an umbrella ready.
In the afternoon the sky is clear. You have to get an umbrella ready.
In the afternoon the sky is cloudy. You don't have to get an umbrella ready.
sentences.notes: 흐리다 → 흐려요: the ㅣ becomes ㅕ before -어요.

sentences.english: If the temperature is low, it is very cold.
sentences.literal: If the temperature is low, very it-is-cold.
distractors: If the temperature is high, it is very cold.
If the temperature is low, it is very hot.
If the temperature is low, it is very warm.
sentences.notes: 낮다 is 'to be low'; its opposite is 높다, 'to be high'.

sentences.english: During the rainy season you have to have an umbrella.
sentences.literal: In the rainy season, an umbrella must-exist.
distractors: During the rainy season you don't need an umbrella.
During the rainy season you have to have a mask.
During winter you have to have an umbrella.
sentences.notes: 장마 is the long rainy season in early summer, usually in June and July.

sentences.english: There will probably be a sudden shower in the afternoon. Be careful.
sentences.literal: In the afternoon a shower come-will. Be-careful.
distractors: There will probably be a sudden shower in the morning.
There will probably be clear skies in the afternoon.
There was a sudden shower in the afternoon.
sentences.notes: 소나기 is a short, heavy shower that stops quickly - not 장마.

sentences.korean: 감기에는 약을 먹고 찬물을 마시지 마세요.
sentences.romanization: gamgieneun yageul meokgo chanmureul masiji maseyo.
sentences.english: For a cold, take medicine and don't drink cold water.
sentences.literal: For a cold, medicine eat-and, cold water do-not-drink.
distractors: For a cold, take medicine and drink cold water.
For a fever, take medicine and don't drink cold water.
For a cold, don't take medicine and don't drink cold water.
sentences.notes: -지 마세요 is the negative of -(으)세요: 마시세요 → 마시지 마세요.

sentences.english: If you don't feel well, rest.
sentences.literal: If the body is not good, rest-please.
distractors: If you don't feel well, go to work.
If you feel good, rest.
If you don't feel well, don't rest.
sentences.notes: 안 좋다 is softer than 나쁘다 and is the usual way to say 'not feeling well'.

sentences.korean: 감기에 걸렸어요. 그래서 기운이 없어요. 물을 많이 마셔야 해요.
sentences.romanization: gamgie geollyeosseoyo. geuraeseo giuni eopseoyo. mureul mani masyeoya haeyo.
sentences.english: I caught a cold. So I have no energy. I have to drink a lot of water.
sentences.literal: On a cold was-caught. So, energy does-not-exist. Water a lot drink-must.
distractors: I caught a cold. So I have a lot of energy. I have to drink a lot of water.
I caught a cold. So I have no energy. I have to go to work.
I have a fever. So I have no energy. I have to drink a lot of water.
sentences.notes: 감기에 걸리다 is the fixed phrase: literally 'get caught on a cold'.

sentences.english: Sleeping a lot is good for your health.
sentences.literal: If you sleep a lot, it is good for health.
distractors: Sleeping a lot is bad for your health.
Sleeping a little is good for your health.
Eating a lot is good for your health.
sentences.notes: 건강에 좋다 is the set phrase for 'good for your health'.

sentences.korean: 오늘은 공기가 나빠요. 마스크를 써야 해요.
sentences.romanization: oneureun gonggiga nappayo. maseukeureul sseoya haeyo.
sentences.english: The air is bad today. You have to wear a mask.
sentences.literal: Today, the air is bad. A mask wear-must.
distractors: The air is good today. You have to wear a mask.
The air is bad today. You don't have to wear a mask.
The water is bad today. You have to wear a mask.
sentences.notes: 나쁘다 → 나빠요. It is the opposite of 좋아요.

sentences.english: When it rains, the air gets better.
sentences.literal: If rain comes, the air becomes-good.
distractors: When it rains, the air gets worse.
When it snows, the air gets better.
When it rains, the air gets cold.
sentences.notes: 좋아지다 = become good; the -지- turns an adjective into a change.

sentences.english: It is a little warm today. I'm going to take a walk.
sentences.literal: Today, a little it-is-warm. A walk do-will.
distractors: It is a little cold today. I'm going to take a walk.
It is a little warm today. I'm not going to take a walk.
It was a little warm yesterday. I took a walk.
sentences.notes: 따뜻하다 → 따뜻해요. It sits between 시원해요 and 더워요.

sentences.english: You have to check the forecast and get an umbrella ready.
sentences.literal: The forecast look-at-and, an umbrella prepare-must.
distractors: You have to check the forecast and leave your umbrella at home.
You have to check the forecast and buy a mask.
I checked the forecast and prepared an umbrella.
sentences.notes: 일기예보 is the full word for a weather forecast; 예보 alone is enough here.

dialogue.title: At the pharmacy
dialogue.setting: A customer describes symptoms to a pharmacist in winter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: My head hurts and I have a runny nose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Do you have a fever too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yes, a little. And I feel dizzy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: It's a cold. Please drink a lot of warm water.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: My stomach hurt, so I couldn't eat breakfast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Don't worry. Get a good rest today.

reading.title: Today's weather and your body
reading.ko: 오늘 서울은 구름이 많아요. 오후에는 비가 와요. 기온은 어제보다 낮아요. 바람도 많이 불어요. 그래서 조금 추워요. 내일은 비가 그치고 하늘이 맑아요. 주말에는 따뜻해요. 요즘은 감기가 많이 돌아요. 몸이 안 좋으면 병원에 빨리 가세요. 집에서 푹 쉬고 따뜻한 물을 많이 마시세요. 그리고 잠을 일찍 자세요. 오후에는 우산을 꼭 준비하세요. 휴가에는 따뜻한 곳에서 쉬세요.
reading.en: Today in Seoul there are a lot of clouds. In the afternoon it rains. The temperature is lower than yesterday. The wind is strong too. So it is a little cold. Tomorrow the rain stops and the sky is clear. On the weekend it is warm. These days colds are going around a lot. If you don't feel well, go to the hospital quickly. Rest at home and drink a lot of warm water. And go to bed early. In the afternoon, be sure to have an umbrella ready. During your time off, rest somewhere warm.

questions.q: What is the weather like in Seoul today?
options: Cloudy, with rain in the afternoon
questions.why: 구름이 많아요. 오후에는 비가 와요 = There are many clouds and it rains in the afternoon.

questions.q: What should you do if you don't feel well?
questions.why: 몸이 안 좋으면 병원에 빨리 가세요.

questions.q: What will the weather be like tomorrow?
options: The rain will stop and the sky will be clear
It will be cloudy all day
questions.why: 내일은 비가 그치고 하늘이 맑아요 = Tomorrow the rain stops and the sky is clear.
